Visual identity

Plinth Stack makes enterprise AI infrastructure feel like a readable technical publication. Warm off-white surfaces, nearly black text, cobalt emphasis, fine rules, and modest corner rounding support a dense but orderly product narrative. Schibsted Grotesk Variable carries confident headlines with optical-size and weight axes; JetBrains Mono marks API paths, code, metrics, indices, and status information. A softly painted atmosphere frames the centered hero while a dark three-column request console supplies a concrete product story. Alternating light narrative spreads and dark evidence panels explain inference, evaluations, traces, architecture, security, and quickstart content. Placeholder badges and illustrative-result notices are part of its procurement-facing honesty.

Preserve these details

  • Preserve warm #faf9f5 paper, near-black ink, cobalt #1e44e5 accents, thin neutral rules, restrained corners, and the painted hero atmosphere rather than inventing neon effects.
  • Schibsted Grotesk Variable declares font-weight 400 alongside wght 600/opsz 72 for the hero and wght 600/opsz 40 for section headings. Preserve axes separately instead of flattening declared weight.
  • Keep the hero request/router/response console and its chosen/rejected model reasoning; follow with Results and In Production At before the problem comparison.
  • Retain the long homepage order including Benchmarks, Security, Quote, Customers, Integrations, Quickstart, Changelog, FAQ and CTA. Pricing calculator official imagery represents /pricing, not a homepage section.
  • Trust badges and demo customer results are explicitly placeholders or illustrative figures. No template source claim proves actual certification, residency, retention, training exclusion, model accuracy or live inference.

Page sequence

  1. NavigationBrand, Platform, Pricing, Docs, Customers, Changelog, Talk to us and Start free; distinct desktop, lap, tablet and phone variants.
  2. Hero GroundPainted backdrop, eyebrow, centered headline with cobalt word emphasis, explanatory text, install pill, four metrics, and dark Request/Router/Response console.
  3. ResultsFour illustrative customer-result cards with a replace-with-your-own notice.
  4. In Production AtDense customer-name proof field and illustrative team-count caption.
  5. The ProblemComparison of stitched vendor stack versus unified platform across vendor management, model changes, outages, regressions, cost attribution and invoices.
  6. InferenceNarrative and bullet list beside routing-policy UI with eligibility, costs, latency and evaluation data.
  7. EvalsFailed-gate sample table paired with explanation of graders, CI regression gates, drift detection and golden cases.
  8. ObservabilityTrace narrative beside spend-by-route and model-share interface; demo amounts are illustrative.
  9. ArchitectureSix numbered steps: Request, Route, Call, Check, Return, Record, with connected graphic and retention detail.
  10. Built ForFour audience tabs and contextual explanation; source opening state shows AI product teams and an evaluation panel.
  11. BenchmarksModel comparison evidence section with quality/performance positioning and sample numbers.
  12. SecurityData-use and enterprise procurement narrative with certification placeholder badges and Trust Center link.
  13. QuoteCustomer quotation presented as template content, not verified endorsement.
  14. CustomersCustomer-story cards with illustrative results and sample company identities.
  15. IntegrationsProvider and tool integration narrative describing a base-URL change.
  16. QuickstartFirst-call explanation and editable code with syntax-colored spans.
  17. ChangelogDated product-change links with compact heading and metadata.
  18. FAQQuestion-and-answer component group addressing first evaluation concerns.
  19. CTAClosing free-start and sales-contact invitation, with painted/veiled background treatment.
  20. FooterProduct, developer, company and legal link groups, brand, rule and bottom metadata; trust links include status and sub-processors.

Responsive and motion

Principal root bands: >=1440px desktop, 1200–1439.98px lap, 810–1199.98px tablet, <=809.98px phone. Component styles add a 640px split. Source Inference/Evals/Observability Wrap changes to column at tablet and phone; several phone Wrap rules use 20px gutters; Architecture/Security section padding changes from declared 115px to 60px. Gutter 32, radius 4 and gap 24 are overall recommendations, not universal measurements.

Source hero word spans declare opacity 0.001, blur(4px) and translateY(14px); the CTA Wrap declares opacity 0 and translateY(16px). Architecture has named scroll markers, Built For tab structures, and FAQ has stateful component variants. No live reveal, copy, tab, or accordion behavior was tested. Recommended recreation: restrained reveals, visible reduced-motion content, keyboard-operable optional tab/accordion controls, and static numbered architecture on small screens.

Suggested timings: 180–280ms interface response and 450–700ms reveals. Source timings are unmeasured. Reduced motion should show all text and stop continuous movement.
